By Tadesse Shanko

The development effort Burkina Faso is showing today, within the limited configuration of Sahelian states where military coups have taken place and foreign military bases have been uprooted, is not an event that says the time has come to declare that democracy is no better a system than authoritarianism when it is compared with the worm-eaten rulers who climbed to power in the name of democracy. Nor does the report that Rodrigo Duterte — who is in the hands of the International Criminal Court in the Netherlands — won the mayoral election in his home city by a landslide convey the message that fighting crime and drugs by lawful means or by extra-legal means "amounts to the same thing / suits us." What both events tell us is that the absurdity of our world is losing all measure. Alongside the glaring agony in Haiti, Congo-Kinshasa, Sudan, the Middle East and Ukraine, Mother History, comparing the prosecutorial zeal the world court has fastened on Duterte, is showing us how much our world has made a laughing stock of itself. History is bitterly mocking the fact that the world's democracy, its fairness, its protection of human rights and its human compassion are becoming one empty husk after another.

- In the few days up to 8 Ginbot (2017 E.C.), what we saw stirring inside the puzzling belly of our world was a golden opportunity that made one ask whether it was a dream or something that might become real. Although Donald Trump is known to be a man capable of political and diplomatic acrobatics, I doubt anyone expected the bending and leaping we saw during the days he visited the Gulf states of the Middle East. His friction with Benjamin Netanyahu, and the favourable outlook he showed towards Yemen, Syria and Iran, are in some people's view superficial and temporary. But if we relate the accumulated weariness within existing conditions to Trump's thirst to loom large in America and in the world as an unforgettable golden leader of history, there is a good thing that could come about even beyond what has already happened.

The war being waged against the Palestinians by way of the struggle Israel has engaged in with Hamas has grown into a planned collective assault that was meant to be prolonged. For assisting in this, America's name has been tarnished in the world. That tarnish had also thinned the friendship of the Gulf Arab states. As a consequence of Israel's Netanyahu losing all measure and any stopping point in the fighting, the peace of the Red Sea has been muddied and the safety of maritime transport and trade has been battered. Israelis themselves are wearied and embarrassed by a merciless war that has found no cut-off. Beyond the fact that Netanyahu's government is known to be a coalition standing without majority support, the recent letter written to Trump by a limited number of Israelis pleading with him to stop the war is one indication of the weariness and the shame at the war's lack of measure. Criticism has repeatedly been voiced among well-known scholars of international relations that America, which ought to be listened to in its capacity as a superpower patron, has instead become the one tuned by Israel. Netanyahu's refusal to take advice has strengthened that criticism. With the understanding between the two muddied and Netanyahu sulking, Trump was seen making his own "mutual-respect" "understanding" with the Houthis of Yemen.

In this situation, Trump's being able to repair the comradeship America had with the Gulf countries — one that had grown tired over time — to the point of sowing new life into it, is no small matter. A two-sided trade and investment agreement counted in a few trillions of dollars (and one glittering with gifts) was concluded: it reduced to some degree the reproach that Trump had made America friendless, and more than made up for the scandal that went as far as the cancellation of aircraft orders placed with Boeing because of the trade war with China. Along with this came the favourable attitude Trump showed towards Syria's and Yemen's recovery as countries and his agreeing to lift the long-standing American sanctions on Syria, as well as the report that they were close to reaching an agreement with Iran stopping short of its becoming a nuclear-weapons owner — all of which improved Trump's image in the Arab world and in the West. There was, and still is, a possible chance of obtaining an even greater result. Because tying a deal with Iran and reaching an understanding has a thread connected to the Israel-Palestine trouble, thinking of a peace solution broadly and at length in that direction would indirectly have the effect of neutralising the Houthis of Yemen, Hezbollah and all other related anti-American and anti-Israeli hostilities; and on the other hand, since Trump, who clashed with a Netanyahu abandoned by domestic support, has support inside Israel, even if he were merely to champion in general terms the creation of a platform for a solution of coexistence — one in which the war has stopped and extremist warmongers on both the Jewish and the Palestinian side are out of the game — being a figure concerned for the peace of both Palestinians and Israelis, the hearing he could obtain on the international stage would count, for every side, as a blessing come down from heaven.

Living startled awake amid the destruction and chaos brought by war and conflict, and in the fear of revenge and counter-revenge, has sickened everyone. And so it has long been everyone's yearning that the Israel-Palestine trouble be resolved and that the surrounding region attain peace and stability. Championing durable peace, in itself, beyond being a contextual force for stopping the war, could send Netanyahu and his like out of government in Israel and bring the forces of peace to power. Nor would the matter of reaching a solution of coexistence necessarily fail, deadlocked as in the old days in an unbridgeable mutual stubbornness. Because the reality of the region has been pleading like a prayer, in hopelessness, for a solution. And so the chance of the two sides drawing together through give-and-take is a very hopeful possibility.

Even if results were not achieved at once, if a peace-loving situation could be created in which both sides and their supporters make sincere efforts towards a peaceful outcome and keep away from war and conflict, that alone would be a great success for the region. And there would be many who would cherish this precious success so that it does not evaporate again. In particular, the era in which the Palestinians are deluded by adventurism — whether it arises from within or comes from outside saying "I am your champion" — has ended. Whether the realisation of the opportunity came fast or slow, had Trump done everything possible to bring it to this stage, that role alone would have dimmed his other weaknesses and become a historic monument making his name famous.

We have come to say all this not because we believe in the individual's good faith. (We have observed just how much good faith the individual has, when he deports destitute migrants from America lumped together with criminals while telling wealthy South African Afrikaners — descendants of the Dutch — whom the racist system privileged, "come to me.") What prompted us is that we saw a golden globe fall into his pocket — one that raises the search for peace — beyond merely saying "what is happening to the Palestinians concerns us… we want peace to be made." That is: his refusal to be steered by Netanyahu's wishes; the fact that our present worldly moment has given us no better lord than him as a hope for peace; the fact that Trump's desire to be known, beyond being "the father of America's resurrection," also as a father of peace, and to multiply the members of the "Abraham Accords," makes him eager; the fact that the fruit of effort that lies within a long thirst for peace has today a riper chance than ever of growing into a graspable peace; and also the fact that the weight the Gulf countries carry is not too small to press for this precious and ripe chance of peace to come by way of their friend Trump.

The value of this graspable opportunity for the Middle East and for the world is as great as resolving three-quarters of a century of trouble. Trump, who wants his name always to be mentioned, has not realised that a golden globe of history fit for this is in his hand. Indeed, he is becoming another example of the sort of mockery by Mother History described in our introduction. Trump has proved unable to rebuke the Israeli leader, who threatens to wreck by force the approaching agreement between Trump and Iran on the nuclear issue and who has refused to let the Palestinians' agony subside. Worse still, he was seen to be pained more by the condemnation of cruelty taking place in American universities such as Harvard than by the killing of innocents in Gaza and by a famine punishment worse than people trampling over one another to scramble for bread; and to be more inflamed by an attack committed outside government on a few whites in South Africa than by the felling of Palestinians counted in the fifty-thousands. He registered his desire to be famous beyond the grave with unforgettable irony. The peace effort that upholds coexistence in mutual respect after dropping enmity, and the completion of "Abraham Accords" membership, have perhaps come to a standstill. Although it was said on 18 Ginbot 2017 E.C. that Hamas was willing to agree to a 60-day ceasefire proposal, said to have been presented by the American side and conditioned on the release of the remaining hostages, the Israeli government's response was that there would be no ceasefire unless Hamas exits its military role and Trump's plan is implemented. In short, what Netanyahu told the Palestinians and the world flatly is that he will not turn back without embittering the Palestinians with collective assault, or uprooting them by scattering them. While cruelty swaggered to this extent, Trump did not utter a word. To the extent that he watched in silence as Netanyahu waved and made use of the plan Trump had presented for Gaza, his name will be unforgettable within a history of cruelty in which he designed and supported the idea of uprooting the Palestinians from Gaza.

At the UN Security Council meeting held on 20 Ginbot 2017 E.C. concerning the delivery of aid to the Palestinians, the representatives of America and of Israel were reading out a lullaby over the cruel Gaza war. Out of a presentation of the Palestinians' agony delivered in a struggle against tears, what the Israeli representative "heard" was a speech fanning antisemitism. The American representative too, while expounding on Israel's right to defend itself, on Hamas having to be defeated, and on the full release of the hostages, did not speak a single sentence about the Palestinians' inviolable right to live in peace in Gaza. To both representatives, the growth of antisemitism seems to come from the mouths that condemned the war; that the cruel war is the chief propagator of antisemitism is not legible to them. Nor did they see that the killing of the two Jewish fiancés in America is, beyond an individual act, chiefly attributable to the war that has found no end.

When one considers the destruction, slaughter and agony the war has caused so far, solution proposals to stop the war are too few, not too many. From this angle, the temporary ceasefire idea over which Netanyahu and Hamas are haggling is like a joke. A solution proposal must be presented that combines the full release of the hostages, Hamas's exit from armed and administrative roles, and the stopping of the war with peaceful coexistence side by side; and Netanyahu and Hamas must be made to face the Palestinian and Israeli peoples and the world community. A solution will come when that happens — one that Israelis, Palestinians and the world community have pressed for and consented to.

The Western powers bustling to impose additional sanctions on the grounds that Putin has heated up the fighting will not escape history's reproach either, so long as their "concerned" sanctions do not look at the Middle East. And so long as the Palestinians' agony continues with no one to stop it, around the Middle East the understanding Trump claims to have set right with the Gulf countries will keep loosening, and the whole "struggle" of putting America first will end up being nothing but a principal — though thankless — servant of the growth of a global market and investment network freed from dependence on America and led by China. The recent ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) meeting held in Malaysia, which involved Middle Eastern countries, pointed to the same thing.

- Had a peace solution been devised for the Middle East trouble, the countries of the region could have created interactions free of side-taking and of the fear of being harnessed. In this respect, the fact that Ethiopia is connected with America, Germany, France, Italy, England, the European Union, China, Russia, India, Turkey, Brazil, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Israel, Qatar, Iran, Pakistan and so on in relationships of common interest that do not make anyone say "she belongs to so-and-so" and on which no political tax is paid, has made Egypt's and Eritrea's web of intrigue go from door to door and glean the leftovers of internal betrayal. In addition, when the Eritrean government is viewed against the fact that Ethiopia has refrained from provocation and is the hope of the Horn region where development is bubbling up, the fact that it is a bandit frozen in time (stuck at 16 Ginbot 1983 E.C.) that is not only an enemy of Ethiopia but even more an enemy of any improvement in the Eritrean people's life is in itself repellent rather than attractive to conspirators. When neighbourhood scraps and abortions thrash about to harm Ethiopia by allying directly or indirectly with the Eritrean tyrant-brigand, what they attack first is their own country's interest; so their effort to harm Ethiopia only degrades them in their own conscienceless. On the other hand, since their attempt to destabilise Ethiopia disturbs the interests of many countries (including the great powers) that are tied to Ethiopia, their quarrel becomes a quarrel with many countries. In other words, beyond the fact that Ethiopia is building a strong state, its being interwoven with many countries in its striding stature has itself become a double security fence for it.

Besides this, the Isaias government, which is serving as the main stirrup for the Egyptian government's intrigue, is a government counting its days, a government that has entered a dragon's mouth. Eritreans scattered across the whole world, driven out by repression and a stunted life, are seeing their opposition grow bitterer and expand rapidly. The remnant groups he has befriended in the belief that they will be useful for hollowing Ethiopia out from within are groups whose politics and popular support are dead, who have sunk from the edge of humanity into criminality, and who chew up again the very people they claim to be fighting for. If there is any difference within this shared character, it is that the Shene found themselves rolling in an ordinary pit of robbers and murderers without noticing when their shrivelled politics evaporated from within them. The Fano are a tailor's sack of many rags — people who have not managed even for one season to learn what politics is, or what an organisation with a design and a strategy is. (It contains everyone: the bellows that flared up holding only "charge!" and that never distinguished whether politics is a broad bean or barley; the one who, in the 21st century, chews over his aristocratic lineage; the poisonous one who cannot tell an ethnic group from an organisation and whom hatred has consumed; the one whose burden is the doctrine that the Amhara are being stripped of their patrimony and dwindling as a people; the political hermit who, with a professorial title dangling, still preaches Leninism.) The TPLF's warmongering remnants, playing with the people's blood, when they failed to disintegrate Ethiopia, long ago died a political death that went as far as attempting the abomination of setting people against people. It was precisely because they knew they were political corpses, and understood that they could no longer bake their wishes onto the people by means of cadres, that they lodged their separatist desire in Abba Selama's mouth by creating a breakaway church.

The TPLF-led interim administration period that followed the Pretoria Agreement was also the time when the TPLF's political death was made public to the eyes and ears of the people of Tigray, when the people mourned without beating their chests and began to breathe new air. Those among the TPLF who repented of that, however few, and who wanted change, were set apart, and the people were able to see face to face the disgraces steeped in looting, intrigue and cruelty standing naked. The intrigue and obstruction carried out against Getachew Reda's interim administration became a mirror through which the people could grasp by whose intrigue the earlier contributory interim administration had failed, and whose plot it was that had entangled the Defence Forces with the people and made them withdraw. Going further, the people came to observe and understand the TPLF's nature and conduct — from its time in government to its time as a bush fighter — with an eye no longer clouded by praise. Clinging to the Pretoria Agreement and to the crack of freedom that appeared under Getachew Reda's administration, they threw themselves into the struggle for lasting peace, for development and for new change. That the people and the youth advanced this far reflected the old TPLF men's stretcher journey. The old self-styled TPLF, unable to hold a congress approved by the Electoral Board, have adorned their funeral procession. The time when, having considered themselves above the law and swaggered, their deadline expired, the warmongers were struck off by the Electoral Board and the people rejoiced and rejoiced, was likewise the performance of a burial rite. Getachew Reda's interview with Fana Television and his plan to establish a new party can be said to have been the beginning of a feast that will bring together long-standing and newly arrived seekers of change. The petition that Debretsion and his colleagues wrote to the African Union was also the voice of a death-rattle spirit coming out of the grave.

If the TPLF as politics and as an organisation has given up its soul and been buried, then what are the people who fantasise about opening a war using Shaebia as cover? Criminals smeared with looting and cruelty. What did these criminals want to fight for, and by giving up what? By offering Ethiopia's and Tigray's interest as a bribe, by giving away as a gift the gold they scrape out of Tigray, by awarding Tigray to Eritrea as a buffer strip of land, by conscripting Tigrayan youth as a blood fence of fighters — all to save their pack-animal lives. Can such people of betrayal and crime mobilise manpower and, sheltered by Shaebia, harm Ethiopia?

Around the time of the international technology expo Ethiopia recently hosted, the sky show performed with 1,500 drones, presented jointly by INSA and the Artificial Intelligence Institute, was not only a demonstration of the design to make Addis Ababa the centrepiece of technology expos. It was also a show that pointed out how much this era's warfare uses information and new technology, and how far apart Ethiopia and Eritrea stand in this respect. Although the Isaias government, which has dried Eritrea up as a country starved of technology and development, may obtain Egyptian assistance, since it is thinned out by opposition and emigration in terms of political acceptance, if its opponents do their work of agitating and awakening for change properly, the war it launches on Ethiopia will be its own farewell. Because its chance of heating up its army politically and conducting an organised battle has narrowed, it is inevitable that the army will crumble and leave the battlefield, or else mutiny.

Our own pack animals, too, far from subsidising Isaias's war with the blood of Tigrayan youth, are wooden pots that cannot even save themselves. This is not a guess. The armed youth who have long been pouring out from the war-worshippers' camp as it crumbles, into the "free land," and who have risen to fight them, are an example of this. The recent entry into the "free land" of two of Debretsion's escorts carrying his dossiers and computer also suggests that the process will continue, and may even intensify to the point of leaving the chiefs of betrayal and crime without an army and of putting them in chains.

For this to become real, however, further work is expected. The acts of vengeance the criminals devoted to serving Isaias have already begun — gnawing at minerals and starving the Ethiopian and Tigrayan market while pouring them into Eritrea, taking revenge on the people who spat them out — must be brought to an end. In a manner that does not provoke war, the necessary security force must be filled out, the interim administration consolidated, and law and order established in Tigray. The organs of justice, offices and commercial activity need to be freed from being the playthings of bullies. It is crucial that the breath of freedom of the Tigrayan people, undisturbed by the lawless and by renegades, marches in a direction that makes Tigray's recovery and change flourish. The people whom the warmongers hold hostage as a fallback must also be helped to escape their palms and to get this chance.

This will be set right only if the forces of peace and change cooperate and manage to organise the youth. Besides this, since a politics of change that carries the peoples' hunger for democracy, for justice and for a better life breaks warmongers' spines more than a cannon does, the forces of change and of peace in Tigray and in Eritrea ought to open a strengthened and united movement. If these things are sharpened, the Eritrean government's plot to strike us with ourselves will become a wilted thing. Nor do I fear that it will have the capacity to create a complicated trap in the future. Indeed, it seems to me that one day I will rise from my bed and find things so changed that what I saw yesterday I will not find the next morning. What emboldens me to say this is that the Ethiopian government's approach is one that has learned from experience and that has the cleverness to isolate, neutralise and defuse dangers. Resting on this, I am confident that it will not enter a protracted war in which both Ethiopian and Eritrean soldiers become great sacrifices.

- Thanks to relatives and comradeship, I learned from childhood what domestic slavery looked like for both men and women, and how much the landlord's lordship consisted of courtyard escorts and bowing (having partaken in the hand-kissing myself). Passing from that kind of concrete knowledge through many experiences of ups and downs, I believe I am fortunate to have lived to see the chapter in which my country has sparkled with a multifaceted beginning of change. Equally, the fact that this striding beginning that is wrenching Ethiopia out of poverty and backwardness has been paid for with bitter loss of human life and destruction of property pours sorrow onto my joy. And when one considers that what exposed us to a massive sacrifice of life and property was a distortion of mental structure formed over long periods and over thirty years, and that our elite "wealth" has been unable to carry out a renaissance work capable of taming this structure and lightening our losses, the sorrow takes on a scorching content. Being myself part of the elite's poverty and idleness, watching powerlessly as history balances its accounts by mowing people down with people, I have gone back and forth in the ungraspable wish that history had a soul and compassion.

The debt-paying of ordinary people and of the youth that I saw in my country I have also seen being settled in Africa through war, migration and death. I have seen it in Europe too. The obsession of clinging to the West that settled on Zelensky and his like — how much suffering it has counted up for Ukrainians! Zelensky's obsession is beating its drum in Taiwan as well. Although Africa has the dream of becoming a united continental country, it is still not far from being seen in the eyes of the powers as a virgin land for scrambling over raw resources. The obstacles that have kept us within this contempt are internal more than external. It is we ourselves, in our weakness, who permit the powers to extend their plundering hands by seducing our states and our politicians with various interests and setting them at odds.

Because the fact that coming to power is a trust to lift up the people's life has not been properly grounded, power is seen as a harvest field of salary for leaders. That criminals and bandits climb to power and, in order to protect their own plundering interest and to escape accountability, turn the people into firewood for battle, is a problem still present in Africa today. If the elite want secession, they will not refrain from riding the people with a false consciousness — "we are fighting for your freedom" — and with armed struggle. There is in Africa the base cunning of igniting conflict and chaos in a neighbouring country and building one's own country by scooping up mineral wealth amid the crisis. Straining to kindle war rather than striving to reconcile conflicts of interest through discussion is a mark of manliness in our Africa. Problems like these are the holes through which the powers, buying servants with perks, intensify their scramble for raw resources. In view of these shames of ours, it is chiefly we ourselves who make it easy for Africa to be seen as a land of dependency where the agony of peoples recurs.

I understand that Ethiopia has drawn lessons from its own, from Africa's and from the world's political ups and downs. Still, there is a puzzle that both Ethiopia and Africa have yet to solve.

Let us not fool ourselves with slogan words such as "man was born free" and "human rights are natural endowments; they are neither given nor taken away." Man has been seen to be a slave both bodily and in conscience. There was a time when human rights were not even known to exist. Even in the era when they were known, they have gone on being trampled. To show this we need not go back as far as the era when human beings were chained slaves. To be a blind applauder of a rule that governs by binding people in poverty and in mental stunting is slavery. To praise as freedom a separatism that has not brought one into economic and political freedom is slavery. To agitate in a way that makes party and people inseparable, and to declare that criticism and attack directed at a party is directed at the people, is the act of chaining the people's conscience and making it an instrument, a slave.

If we Africans were to treat democratic freedoms as the right to live within "natural freedoms," we would fail to get beyond "seeing them as custom." If we cheapen democracy by treating freedom of speech and the freedom to demonstrate and to strike as mere relishes, democracy will not stay with us like an ornament of custom. Using free discussion, free writing and free assembly as tools, drawing ideas and hearts closer and moving as one force, we have very many tasks we ought to accomplish. Moreover, our democratic institutional capacity and our capacity to grind idea against idea are weak and need care. If we forget these two things — if the group in power and its opponents cannot exert themselves on these tasks; if the one in power is engrossed in schemes to prolong its power, while the opponents are absorbed in the short goal of unsettling or overthrowing the group in power by multiplying and inciting the people's grievances about the shortcomings of life — then it is inevitable that our democratic and constitutional life becomes a scuffle. The turbulence can go from the field of speech and of newspapers all the way to the gun.

Unless we elites clearly identify the social problems and distortions that create division, wounding and friction, and work together to ease them through progress and fairness and to strengthen our common we-ness, and unless we succeed in making contests of ideas that can live together the normal reality of our country's politics (if our political context is shaken by contradictory interests), our democracy will be exposed to becoming an empty husk. And as an empty husk it will have no lifespan. It will become a thing that keeps being torn apart and nullified through military coups and violence.

If one falls into the vortex of endless wrangling in the name of democracy, it will be hard to crawl out of a life without change. While crawling and being tossed about in changelessness, a politician-hood that revolves within the custom of exposing violations of democracy and of human rights, instead of devising a way to help one another out of that fall, is useless ignorance. An authoritarianism that bursts in and tears apart such a vortex of life quickly gains popular support when it sets development moving, because the people's previously broken hope turns to seeing a bright tomorrow. History has seen a reality in which development advanced under authoritarianism and in which people and government fitted together. It cannot be said that this will not occur today either. Politicians of industry-less countries (whether on our continent or outside it) who have not properly examined this puzzle and have not marched together will not escape being trapped in a vortex of crisis and a life of stumbling.

The African Union is a union caught in this kind of puzzle. The reality in which democratic constitutionalism is bent by deceitful amendment of articles and becomes an instrument of power-lovers is not alien to our Africa. To say "I was elected" from one election period to the next, whether by tripping up competitors with various tactics or by soiling the electoral process with frauds, is an abomination no less than carrying out a coup at every election period. Seeing rulers who prolong their power through this abomination is nothing rare for us in Africa. Because of these thieves of power, there is in Africa the distressing reality in which the arrival of an election season means the arrival of a time of turmoil, disorder and gunfire. We find thieves who proclaim electoral victory through fraudulent methods and rob power to the sound of applause seated in the African Union as constitutional leaders. The union has no eye that distinguishes a sham constitutional transfer of power from the real thing. That the union embraces rulers who rob power through sham elections while stripping recognition and membership from those who took power outside elections (even when the people's ululation and hope for change are with them) is a puzzle of the union that needs a solution. How do we help countries and politicians so that democratic constitutionalism is not shaken by vote-robbery and not cut short by violence and coups? And how do we approach and help those rays of change who came by a route that violated the constitution and who have exerted themselves to stir the people's life, so that they do not darken and so that they enter the road of democratic constitutionalism? These two questions need substantive answers that accomplish more than adjusting an institutional article.

Let us focus on Ethiopia. The ploughing farmer cuts his furrow knowing and observing where his field ends. The leadership of a political party and of a government is expected to be like that. When

a5874.t:
The Minister of Defence and Veterans Affairs, Frans Kapofi, is satisfied with the achievement of Exercise Hanganee 2 in fostering interactions and cultural practises among Namibian and Botswana defence forces.
The forces rendered humanitarian assistance in various parts of the Omaheke Region.
Kapofi made the remark at the closing ceremony of Operation Hanganee 2 at Tsjaka settlement in the Kalahari Constituency, which started from the 15th to the 30th of June.
The Namibian Defence Minister says that the exercise provided an opportunity to deepen the country's bilateral relations.
Kapofi also added that the operation will strengthen military-to-military cooperation.
"Apart from issues related to military relations, this exercise contributed immensely to the wellbeing of the community through outreach programmes such as provisional health services, basic necessities, and cleaning campaigns, to mention but a few. It is now my single honour and privilege to declare Exercise Hanganee 2 officially closed."
Exercise Co-Director, Brigadier Anderson Matlho of the Botswana Defence Force, acknowledged the commitment and dedication shown by officers of both countries during the exercise.
"If I didn't recognise and appreciate the hard work demonstrated by exercise planners to put this exercise together, it is always not easy to achieve maximum desirable results from people coming from different backgrounds, but we maintain the same spirit and work ethic as we came to conclude this exercise."
The army forces also assisted with the renovation of and setting up of a playground at Mphe Tuto Primary School in Tsjaka.

a5956.t:
O Burkina Faso, governado há quase três anos por uma junta, é prejudicado pelos ataques mortais de grupos armados terroristas afiliados à Al-Qaida e ao Estado Islâmico.
"O Grupo de Apoio ao Islão e aos Muçulmanos (GSIM), afiliado à Al-Qaida, atacou a cidade de Djibo, na região do Sahel, em 11 de maio, e a vila de Youba, na região norte, no dia 03 de Agosto, matando pelo menos 40 civis", disse a HRW num comunicado.
"O Estado Islâmico do Sahel (EI) atacou um comboio civil que entregava ajuda humanitária à cidade sitiada de Gorom Gorom, na região do Sahel, em 28 de Julho, matando pelo menos nove civis", acrescentou.
Os habitantes da aldeia de Youba explicaram à HRW que os extremistas quiseram "punir a comunidade local por não ter obedecido às instruções do GSIM de abandonar algumas colheitas" .
Numa resposta à HRW no dia 15 de Agosto, o GSIM assegurou "nunca ter como alvo intencionalmente civis", mencionando "alegações infundadas", ou "no máximo, incidentes causados por balas perdidas", dos quais dizem não ter conhecimento.
A pesquisadora da HRW especialista no Sahel Ilaria Allegrozzi estima que "as autoridades devem garantir uma melhor proteção a todos os civis em perigo".
Ao assumir o poder no final de Setembro de 2022, o chefe da junta, o capitão Ibrahim Traoré, prometeu restabelecer a segurança em poucos meses, mas os ataques - que visam soldados e civis - não diminuíram.
A HRW pede que as autoridades "investiguem os abusos, particularmente aqueles cometidos pelos militares e milícias aliadas, e processem judicialmente os responsáveis".
A ONG observa que "o Governo tem cada vez mais atacado civis durante operações" antiterroristas.
O exército buukinabé e os seus auxiliares civis, os Voluntários para a Defesa da Pátria (VDP), são regularmente acusados por ONG, incluindo a HRW, de cometer massacres de civis.
A organização Acled, que contabiliza as vítimas de conflitos no mundo, relata mais de 26 mil pessoas mortas em ataques terroristas - civis e militares - desde 2015 no Burkina Faso, sendo mais de metade nos últimos três anos.
Foto: depositphotos
a5956.en:
Burkina Faso, governed for almost three years by a junta, is beset by deadly attacks from armed terrorist groups affiliated with Al-Qaeda and the Islamic State.

"The Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (GSIM), affiliated with Al-Qaeda, attacked the town of Djibo, in the Sahel region, on 11 May, and the village of Youba, in the northern region, on 3 August, killing at least 40 civilians," HRW said in a statement.

"The Islamic State in the Sahel (IS) attacked a civilian convoy delivering humanitarian aid to the besieged town of Gorom Gorom, in the Sahel region, on 28 July, killing at least nine civilians," it added.

Residents of the village of Youba explained to HRW that the extremists wanted to "punish the local community for not having obeyed GSIM's instructions to abandon certain crops".

In a response to HRW on 15 August, GSIM maintained that it "never intentionally targets civilians", speaking of "unfounded allegations", or "at most, incidents caused by stray bullets", of which it says it has no knowledge.

HRW researcher and Sahel specialist Ilaria Allegrozzi considers that "the authorities must guarantee better protection for all civilians in danger".

On taking power at the end of September 2022, the junta leader, Captain Ibrahim Traore, promised to restore security within a few months, but the attacks - which target both soldiers and civilians - have not diminished.

HRW calls on the authorities to "investigate the abuses, particularly those committed by the military and allied militias, and to prosecute those responsible".

The NGO observes that "the Government has increasingly attacked civilians during" counterterrorism operations.

The Burkinabe army and its civilian auxiliaries, the Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland (VDP), are regularly accused by NGOs, including HRW, of committing massacres of civilians.

The organisation Acled, which counts the victims of conflicts around the world, reports more than 26,000 people killed in terrorist attacks - civilians and military - since 2015 in Burkina Faso, more than half of them in the last three years.

Photo: depositphotos

a6404.t:
The International Organisation for Migration (IOM) has tipped Malawi to enhance collaboration to curb irregular migration, which is apparently rampant in the country but underreported.
IOM Chief of Mission to Malawi Nomagugu Ncube made the remarks during the handover of a patrol vessel in Nkhata Bay to the Department of Immigration and Citizenship Services.
Ncube said surveys the organisation conducted recently revealed that irregular migration and trafficking in persons exist, but the figures it has are not a true reflection of what is on the ground.
She said this is because the main means of operation by smugglers and traffickers is to avoid detection, hence the numbers are scanty.
“I would say Malawi is doing well but it can do more in the sense that the government recognises there is an irregular migration challenge.
- Advertisement -
“The second thing is to enhance collaboration among actors. For instance, the government is engaging the government of Mozambique to promote the use of a border pass so that people can move between the two countries regularly without using passports,” Ncube said.
Among other things, Ncube also said IOM is aware of the issue of passports and urged the government to address it quickly so that it can facilitate regular migration.
The ‘Immigration Patrol Vessel’ has been donated by the Japanese Government through IOM under the immigration’s Enhancing Border Security and Regular Migration project.
Japanese Ambassador to Malawi Yoichi Oya hoped the vessel would enhance migration management around lakeshore districts.
- Advertisement -
- Advertisement -
“Japan is a strong advocate for the concept of human security, emphasising the protection and empowerment of individuals and communities from various threats. This approach is deeply integrated into Japan’s foreign policy and development assistance,” he said.
In his remarks, Fletcher Nyirenda, Commissioner responsible for Operations at the Department of Immigration, acknowledged that their visibility was mostly on land and at airports.

a6571.t:
Projekt der US-Regierung unterstützt Jugendliche
Windhoek (cr) • Im Herzen von Windhoek gelegen, brummt die Bäckerei Mello vor Aktivität. Der 24-Stunden-Betrieb, in dem täglich Tausende von Broten hergestellt werden, ist seit kurzem der Arbeitsplatz der jungen Rosamunde, einer Teilnehmerin des von der US-Regierung finanzierten Projekts „Reach Namibia“. Die 23-Jährige lebt mit ihrer Mutter und ihren Geschwistern in Ombili, einem Wohngebiet am Stadtrand von Windhoek, wo sie von einer Nachbarin von der Initiative erfuhr.
,Reach Namibia' wurde im August 2023 gegründet und bietet umfassende Gesundheits- und Sozialdienste für HIV-gefährdete Kinder, Jugendliche und junge Erwachsene an, um ihnen Lebenskompetenzen zu vermitteln und den Zugang zu Bildung, Arbeit und Gesundheitsdiensten zu verbessern. ,Reach Namibia' wird vom „US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief“ (PEPFAR) über die „United States Agency for International Development“ (USAID) finanziert und von „Project HOPE Namibia“ und „Intrahealth Namibia“ durchgeführt.
Rosamunde absolvierte erfolgreich eine Schulung zur Verbesserung der wirtschaftlichen Sicherheit junger Frauen, in der sie finanzielle Kenntnisse, Professionalität, Kommunikation, Führungsqualitäten und die Vorbereitung auf den Arbeitsmarkt (einschließlich Verfassen von Lebensläufen und Fähigkeiten für Vorstellungsgespräche) erlernte. Auch Berufsausbildungskurse wie Klempner, Maurer und Bäcker werden unterstützt. „Die 23-Jährige entschied sich für den Backkurs und schloss ihr Praktikum in der Bäckerei Mello mit Bravour ab“, so die Amerikanische Botschaft.
Die Inhaber der Bäckerei, Dylan Maritz und Mike Samson, unterstützen das Programm ,Reach Namibia', indem sie vielversprechenden Absolventen Praktika und Stellen anbieten. Darüber hinaus geben sie den Programmmitarbeitern wichtige Einblicke und Informationen, um sicherzustellen, dass die Ausbildungskurse den tatsächlichen Bedürfnissen und Gegebenheiten des Arbeitsmarktes des Landes entsprechen.
Rosamunde beschreibt sich selbst als fröhlich und glücklich, da sie nun einen Job hat, der dazu beiträgt, ihre Verwandten zu Hause zu unterstützen, indem er Ausgaben wie Lebensmittel und Hygieneartikel deckt. Sie nutzt auch ein Existenzgründungspaket mit einem Gasherd und Backutensilien, das ihr vom Projekt ,Reach Namibia' zur Verfügung gestellt wurde, um am Wochenende zu backen und Brot an Mitglieder der örtlichen Gemeinschaft zu verkaufen.

a6571.en:
A project of the US government supports young people

Windhoek (cr) • Located in the heart of Windhoek, the Mello bakery is buzzing with activity. The 24-hour operation, which produces thousands of loaves of bread every day, has recently become the workplace of young Rosamunde, a participant in the US-government-funded project “Reach Namibia”. The 23-year-old lives with her mother and her siblings in Ombili, a residential area on the outskirts of Windhoek, where she learned about the initiative from a neighbour.

'Reach Namibia' was founded in August 2023 and offers comprehensive health and social services for children, adolescents and young adults at risk of HIV, in order to teach them life skills and improve their access to education, work and health services. 'Reach Namibia' is funded by the “US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief” (PEPFAR) through the “United States Agency for International Development” (USAID) and is implemented by “Project HOPE Namibia” and “Intrahealth Namibia”.

Rosamunde successfully completed a training course to improve the economic security of young women, in which she learned financial knowledge, professionalism, communication, leadership qualities and preparation for the labour market (including writing CVs and interview skills). Vocational training courses such as plumber, bricklayer and baker are also supported. “The 23-year-old chose the baking course and completed her internship at the Mello bakery with flying colours,” according to the American Embassy.

The owners of the bakery, Dylan Maritz and Mike Samson, support the 'Reach Namibia' programme by offering internships and positions to promising graduates. In addition, they give the programme staff important insights and information to ensure that the training courses correspond to the actual needs and conditions of the country's labour market.

Rosamunde describes herself as cheerful and happy, since she now has a job that helps to support her relatives at home by covering expenses such as food and hygiene products. She also uses a start-up package with a gas stove and baking utensils, provided to her by the 'Reach Namibia' project, to bake at the weekend and sell bread to members of the local community.

a6621.t:
De grandes réalisations annoncées avant la fin de l’année 
La quatrième  session  ordinaire du Conseil d’Administration  du Millénium challenge account (Mca-Bénin) s’est tenue hier  au siège de l’institution sis  à Cotonou. A l’occasion, plusieurs grandes nouvelles réalisations ont été annoncées… 
entre octobre et décembre 2008 et prendront en compte  les quatre Projets du Mca, à savoir « Accès au foncier », « Accès  aux services  financiers », « Accès à la justice » et «Accès  aux marchés » Environ 225090677 dollars Us seront investis  dans diverses  activités et réalisations du  Programme Millénium challenge account Bénin  (Mca-Bénin), d’octobre à décembre 2008.  La quatrième session  ordinaire  du Conseil d’administration  du Mca Bénin, tenue hier à Cotonou  a été consacrée à   l’examen  et l’adoption du Plan de travail proposé.   Tous les quatre projets du Mca Bénin devront connaître de nouvelles réalisations  d’ici à la fin de l’année.   A l’ouverture des travaux, le  Coordonnateur   du Mca-Bénin, Pierre Simon Adovèlandé  a fourni tous les détails nécessaires à travers  une présentation exhaustive de ce plan à l’assistance. Ainsi, pour  les quatre projets, à savoir,  « Accès au foncier », « Accès  aux services  financiers », « Accès à la justice » et «Accès  aux marchés », plusieurs activités sont programmées. Entre autres,  l’organisation  de la restitution  technique des études, la tenue des sessions  des comités techniques,  l’acquisition  d’équipements  pour la nouvelle Commission Ph/Tf; la sélection   de 110 villages de la phase 2, l’aménagement  des locaux  devant  abriter les bureaux  des centres départementaux  la mise à disposition des mobiliers  à l’Ecole nationale  d’administration et de la magistrature (Enam) ;  le démarrage des travaux de construction du centre  d’informations juridiques ;  vote  par l’Assemblée nationale des codes ; l’obtention  des titres de propriétés des sites de construction  des juridictions ; la mise en œuvre des  recommandations  de l’audit   financier au Port autonome de Cotonou, l’acquisition  d’un remorqueur, réalisation des formalités  d’identification  des équipements   au niveau du Port … D’autres activités sont également prévues, telles que l’organisation de plusieurs séances publiques avec les acteurs de la société  civile , les Ong et autres partenaires sociaux sur  les composantes et l’ évolution du Programme Mca –Bénin. 
 Comme on le constate,  l’année  3  s’annonce très intensive  pour le Mca-Bénin et marque en même temps  le top de la phase  la plus attendue de son programme. « C’est  la période de l’enclenchement des grands efforts et des grands défis » a déclaré hier  le Coordonnateur national. Si  la première  et la seconde année ont été mises à profit pour lancer le programme, il est maintenant question de passer à la vitesse de  croisière, selon Mr Adovèlandé, qui n’a pas manqué de remercier tous les partenaires dans ce programme pour l’éminent rôle qu’ils y jouent. Il a aussi  salué  l’engagement da la partie américaine  à travers  le Millénium Challenge Coorporation , ayant  contribué à faire accélérer les  activités déjà réalisées.
Le Président du Conseil d’Administration du Mca -Bénin, Mr Nestor Dako, n’a pas caché, non plus,  sa joie et sa profonde  gratitude  par rapport aux différents  acquis   de ce programme. « L’année qui s’annonce est une année charnière et celle des grandes réalisations  qui assurent une plus grande  visibilité  au Programme Mca-Bénin » a – t- il aussi souligné. Les activités et diverses tâches   prévues au niveau des Directions» Evaluation  des impacts  environnemental et social », « Suivi évaluation » et «  Communication  et Documentation » ont été également passées  au peigne fin lors de la session ordinaire  d’hier. Il en est de  même pour  le plan financier pluriannuel, le budget détaillé  de l’année 3 et du trimestre 1 de l’année 3 ;  le rapport financier  trimestre 1 de l’année 3 , la demande  de décaissement   des fonds Mcc N°009 ;  le Plan de passation  de marchés pour le trimestre 1 de l’année 3 ;  le rapport cumulé  de progrès  de passation des marchés relatif au décaissement N°009 ;  le Rapport  relatif aux conditions  préalables au Décaissement N%009, les contrats  et engagements signés, décisions  importantes prises et autres actions  initiées par le Coordonnateur national   depuis la dernière  réunion du Ca ; le Plan de suivi-évaluation révisé, etc.
 A la suite  des  débats et ratification  des documents  présentés, plusieurs autres questions  diverses ont été également abordées au cours des assises   comme celles relatives aux implications des engagements  de confidentialité , aux  résultats des  Conseils  et Comités consultatifs et  à l’analyse des difficultés  de mise  en œuvre des  actions de réformes  du Centre de formalités des entreprises.   
Christian Tchanou
Nestor Dako, Président du Conseil  d’administration  du Mca-Bénin
« Le bilan est globalement  positif après les deux années écoulées et je m’en réjouis. C’est un bilan qui mérite d’être salué car il présente des acquis très importants dans l’évolution de ce programme. Je suis de plus  en plus optimiste quant à son aboutissement heureux  au terme des trois  années qui restent.   Je  le suis d’autant plus que les règles  qui gouvernent  les actions au niveau de ce programme demeurent très rigoureuses et sont appliquées par des hommes qui sont également très rigoureux et très dévoués à la tâche. Il ne peut donc pas y avoir de dérives, car  tout est dans un disque compact. Tout y est verrouillé »
Le député Sacca Fikara, membre du Conseil d’administration Mca Bénin
« Ce programme est fortement accompagné par l’Assemblée nationale qui y met tous les moyens  pour jouer la partition qui est la sienne dans sa réussite. L’organisation des études des codes  au Parlement est une préoccupation majeure de tous les députés et nous nous investissons pour  son accélération. Contrairement à ce qui se dit, l’Assemblée nationale  ne pose aucun acte visant à bloquer l’évolution de ce programme, car nos activités  ne se limitent pas seulement aux plénières. Il y a des commissions internes qui travaillent tous les jours sur ce dossier sans grand bruit.  Je tiens à rassurer  toutes les populations, les responsables à divers niveaux et les partenaires impliqués dans ce programme que  les  codes exigés seront votés.  Je  remercie aussi  le Mca pour tout ce qu’il fait au Bénin. »
Patrick  Noyes, Vice-Président de la Ccib et membre du Conseil d’Administration du Mca-Bénin
« Il est nécessaire que la Ccib  contribue fortement  à la réussite  du programme  Mca-Bénin. Ce que nous essayons de faire, car beaucoup de nos éléments  y sont impliqués. Nous insistons surtout sur le foncier qui est l’un des projet importants de ce programme et qui est le socle d’une bonne  politique agricole. En tout cas, l’année 3 comme je le vois ne sera pas de tout repos, car beaucoup d’investissements seront  effectifs. Ce sont là, de très belles nouvelles pour tous les Béninois. »  
Pierre Simon Adovèlandé, Coordonateur national Mca-Bénin
« Il est vrai que nous avons rencontré quelques difficultés, mais nous avons fait du chemin quand même. Notre intervention, en 2 ans, a apporté  beaucoup d’améliorations dans certains secteurs  d’activités du pays, comme le Port autonome de Cotonou, qui aurait pu être déclassé, il y a un an sans l’appui du Mca-Bénin. Il y a aussi de nouvelles pratiques et  acquisitions de titres fonciers qui sont en cours de réalisation. Et d’ici à là, les   Béninois auront la possibilité  d’avoir des titres fonciers  à moins de 200.000 Cfa dans un court délai. Nous avons en tout cas, un programme de 5 ans et nous venons  de boucler  2 ans. Nous ne devons pas donc espérer des résultats immédiats. Je demande aux Béninois  de prendre un peu de patience et ils seront très fiers et très heureux d’être bénéficiaires de ce programme d’ici à là.
a6621.en:
Ordinary session of the MCA-Benin

Major achievements announced before the end of the year

The fourth ordinary session of the Board of Directors of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA-Benin) was held yesterday at the institution's headquarters in Cotonou. On that occasion, several major new achievements were announced...

[They will take place] between October and December 2008 and will cover the four MCA projects, namely "Access to Land", "Access to Financial Services", "Access to Justice" and "Access to Markets". About USD 225,090,677 will be invested in various activities and achievements of the Millennium Challenge Account Benin (MCA-Benin) Programme from October to December 2008. The fourth ordinary session of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin, held yesterday in Cotonou, was devoted to the review and adoption of the proposed work plan. All four MCA-Benin projects are to see new achievements by the end of the year. At the opening of proceedings, the Coordinator of MCA-Benin, Pierre Simon Adovelande, provided all the necessary details through an exhaustive presentation of this plan to those present. Thus, for the four projects - "Access to Land", "Access to Financial Services", "Access to Justice" and "Access to Markets" - several activities are planned. Among others: the organisation of the technical presentation of the studies, the holding of technical committee sessions, the acquisition of equipment for the new Ph/Tf Commission; the selection of 110 villages for phase 2, the fitting out of the premises to house the offices of the departmental centres, the provision of furniture to the National School of Administration and Magistracy (ENAM); the start of construction work on the legal information centre; the adoption of the codes by the National Assembly; obtaining title deeds for the sites where the courts are to be built; the implementation of the recommendations of the financial audit at the Autonomous Port of Cotonou, the acquisition of a tugboat, the completion of equipment identification formalities at the Port... Other activities are also planned, such as the organisation of several public meetings with civil society actors, NGOs and other social partners on the components and progress of the MCA-Benin Programme.

As can be seen, Year 3 promises to be very intensive for MCA-Benin and at the same time marks the start of the most awaited phase of its programme. "This is the period when the great efforts and the great challenges get under way," the national Coordinator declared yesterday. If the first and second years were used to launch the programme, it is now a matter of moving up to cruising speed, according to Mr Adovelande, who did not fail to thank all the partners in this programme for the eminent role they play in it. He also welcomed the commitment of the American side through the Millennium Challenge Corporation, which has helped to accelerate the activities already completed.

The Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin, Mr Nestor Dako, likewise did not hide his joy and his deep gratitude regarding the various gains of this programme. "The coming year is a pivotal year and the year of the major achievements that will give greater visibility to the MCA-Benin Programme," he also stressed. The activities and various tasks planned at the level of the "Environmental and Social Impact Assessment", "Monitoring and Evaluation" and "Communication and Documentation" departments were also gone over with a fine-tooth comb during yesterday's ordinary session. The same applied to the multi-year financial plan, the detailed budget for Year 3 and for Quarter 1 of Year 3; the financial report for Quarter 1 of Year 3, the request for disbursement of MCC funds No. 009; the procurement plan for Quarter 1 of Year 3; the cumulative procurement progress report relating to disbursement No. 009; the report on the conditions precedent to Disbursement No. 009, the contracts and commitments signed, important decisions taken and other actions initiated by the national Coordinator since the last Board meeting; the revised monitoring and evaluation plan, etc.

Following the debates and the ratification of the documents presented, several other miscellaneous matters were also addressed during the proceedings, such as those relating to the implications of confidentiality undertakings, the results of the advisory Councils and Committees, and the analysis of the difficulties in implementing the reform measures of the Business Formalities Centre.

Christian Tchanou

Nestor Dako, Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin

"The record is broadly positive after the two years that have passed and I am pleased about it. It is a record that deserves to be commended because it shows very important gains in the development of this programme. I am increasingly optimistic about its successful conclusion at the end of the three years that remain. I am all the more so because the rules that govern the actions within this programme remain very rigorous and are applied by men who are also very rigorous and very devoted to the task. There can therefore be no abuses, because everything is on a compact disc. Everything in it is locked down."

Deputy Sacca Fikara, member of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin

"This programme is strongly supported by the National Assembly, which is putting all its means into playing its own part in its success. Organising the study of the codes in Parliament is a major concern of all the deputies and we are working to speed it up. Contrary to what is being said, the National Assembly is taking no action aimed at blocking the progress of this programme, because our activities are not limited solely to plenary sittings. There are internal committees working every day on this file without much noise. I want to reassure all the people, officials at various levels and the partners involved in this programme that the required codes will be adopted. I also thank the MCA for everything it is doing in Benin."

Patrick Noyes, Vice-President of the CCIB and member of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin

"It is necessary for the CCIB to contribute strongly to the success of the MCA-Benin programme. That is what we are trying to do, because many of our members are involved in it. We insist above all on land tenure, which is one of the important projects of this programme and which is the foundation of a good agricultural policy. In any case, Year 3, as I see it, will not be at all restful, because a great deal of investment will become effective. This is very good news for all Beninese."

Pierre Simon Adovelande, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin

"It is true that we have encountered some difficulties, but we have nonetheless come a long way. Our intervention, over 2 years, has brought many improvements in certain sectors of activity in the country, such as the Autonomous Port of Cotonou, which could have been downgraded a year ago without the support of MCA-Benin. There are also new practices and acquisitions of land titles that are under way. And between now and then, Beninese people will have the possibility of obtaining land titles for less than 200,000 CFA within a short time. In any case, we have a 5-year programme and we have just completed 2 years. We must not therefore expect immediate results. I ask the Beninese to be a little patient and they will be very proud and very happy to be beneficiaries of this programme by then."

a6684.t:
Segundo comunicou a embaixada todas as pessoas que pretendem solicitar um destes vistos deverão alterar as configurações de privacidade das suas contas nas redes sociais para o modo “público”.
A medida visa, segundo o comunicado da Embaixada, facilitar os processos de verificação necessários para estabelecer a identidade e a admissibilidade dos candidatos ao território norte-americano, conforme previsto na legislação dos EUA.
As categorias F e M dizem respeito, respectivamente, a estudantes em instituições académicas e vocacionais nos Estados Unidos, enquanto os vistos J abrangem participantes em programas de intercâmbio educacional e cultural, incluindo au pairs, professores e investigadores.
Refere-se que Cabo Verde encontra-se na lista de países sob ameaça de restrição de vistos pelos EUA, situação que pode ser contornada se assim como outros países, aceitar receber deportados.
a6684.en:
According to what the embassy communicated, all persons who intend to apply for one of these visas must change the privacy settings of their social media accounts to "public" mode.

The measure aims, according to the Embassy's statement, to facilitate the verification processes necessary to establish the identity and admissibility of applicants to North American territory, as provided for in US legislation.

The F and M categories concern, respectively, students at academic and vocational institutions in the United States, while J visas cover participants in educational and cultural exchange programmes, including au pairs, teachers and researchers.

It is noted that Cabo Verde is on the list of countries under threat of visa restrictions by the US, a situation that can be circumvented if, like other countries, it agrees to receive deportees.

a6731.t:
Le gouvernement malien a exprimé sa surprise et son indignation après la publication, le 15 février dernier, du Département de l’efficacité gouvernementale (DOGE) des États-Unis, annonçant l’annulation d’une subvention de 14 millions de dollars (environ 8,8 milliards FCFA) initialement destinée à soutenir la cohésion sociale au Mali.
Dans un communiqué daté du 24 février 2025, le Ministère des Affaires étrangères et de la Coopération internationale du Mali a tenu à clarifier la position du pays sur cette affaire et à dénoncer une fois de plus l’utilisation de l’aide publique au développement comme « instrument de déstabilisation ».
Le gouvernement malien affirme avoir « saisi les autorités américaines » pour obtenir des explications sur l’annulation de cette subvention, dont l’existence n’avait jusqu’alors pas été officiellement confirmée par les autorités maliennes.
Au-delà de l’annulation de cette aide, Bamako dénonce une pratique plus large, qu’elle estime être une « tentative d’instrumentalisation de l’aide publique pour affaiblir la souveraineté des États africains ».
Le communiqué parvenu à APA rappelle que « bien avant la mise en place de la nouvelle administration américaine, le Mali alertait déjà sur ces dérives », qui, selon les autorités de la Transition, serviraient notamment à « financer des réseaux terroristes opérant au Sahel ».
Dans cette optique, le gouvernement malien avait déjà pris ses distances avec l’USAID. En effet, depuis deux ans, Bamako a refusé de signer l’Accord quinquennal de Subvention d’objectif de développement avec les États-Unis. Plusieurs projets financés par cette agence américaine, y compris ceux liés à la cohésion sociale, ont été mis en pause par le gouvernement malien, qui exige que « toute coopération respecte la souveraineté du pays et les priorités définies par l’État ».
Ce gel des financements étrangers s’inscrit dans la ligne politique défendue par le Président de la Transition, qui a fait de la « restauration de la souveraineté nationale un principe fondamental de gouvernance ».
Le Ministère des Affaires étrangères malien ne se contente pas de dénoncer ces pratiques. Il va plus loin en appelant Washington à engager des poursuites judiciaires contre les responsables de ces détournements de fonds. Selon les autorités maliennes, des sommes destinées au développement du pays auraient été « détournées à des fins subversives et contraires aux besoins essentiels des populations ».
Le communiqué souligne également que « le Mali se reconnaît dans la nouvelle orientation des autorités américaines visant à assainir et à humaniser leurs subventions », tout en insistant sur la nécessité de « prévenir toute utilisation abusive ou contraire à l’intérêt des États bénéficiaires ».
Cette déclaration intervient dans un climat diplomatique fragile. Le Mali, dirigé par une transition militaire depuis 2020, a récemment voté contre une résolution de l’ONU sur l’Ukraine, le même jour que l’annonce du DOGE tout comme la Russie et les États-Unis. Cet épisode marque un nouvel épisode de tensions entre Bamako et ses partenaires occidentaux.
Le gouvernement malien réaffirme son engagement en faveur de la paix et de la stabilité, précisant que la coopération internationale doit se faire sur « la base du respect mutuel et des intérêts réciproques ».
Vers une normalisation des relations ?
Malgré ces tensions, Bamako semble laisser la porte ouverte à un dialogue avec Washington, notamment sur la question des subventions. La reconnaissance par les autorités maliennes de la « prise de conscience des États-Unis sur les risques de détournement » laisse entrevoir une possibilité de réengagement sous de nouvelles conditions.
En attendant, le Mali reste ferme sur ses exigences : « Toute coopération future devra respecter la souveraineté de l’État malien et répondre aux attentes réelles du peuple ».
MD/ac/Sf/APA
a6731.en:
The Malian government expressed its surprise and indignation following the publication, on 15 February, by the United States Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), announcing the cancellation of a $14 million grant (about 8.8 billion CFA francs) originally intended to support social cohesion in Mali.

In a communique dated 24 February 2025, Mali's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation sought to clarify the country's position on this matter and to denounce once again the use of official development assistance as an "instrument of destabilisation".

The Malian government states that it has "approached the American authorities" to obtain explanations for the cancellation of this grant, whose existence had until then not been officially confirmed by the Malian authorities.

Beyond the cancellation of this aid, Bamako denounces a broader practice, which it considers to be an "attempt to instrumentalise public aid in order to weaken the sovereignty of African states".

The communique received by APA recalls that "well before the installation of the new American administration, Mali was already sounding the alarm about these abuses", which, according to the Transition authorities, serve in particular to "finance terrorist networks operating in the Sahel".

With this in mind, the Malian government had already distanced itself from USAID. Indeed, for the past two years Bamako has refused to sign the five-year Development Objective Grant Agreement with the United States. Several projects financed by this American agency, including those linked to social cohesion, have been put on hold by the Malian government, which demands that "all cooperation respect the country's sovereignty and the priorities defined by the State".

This freeze on foreign financing is in line with the political course defended by the President of the Transition, who has made "the restoration of national sovereignty a fundamental principle of governance".

The Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs does not stop at denouncing these practices. It goes further by calling on Washington to bring legal proceedings against those responsible for these misappropriations of funds. According to the Malian authorities, sums intended for the country's development were "diverted for subversive purposes contrary to the essential needs of the population".

The communique also stresses that "Mali recognises itself in the new orientation of the American authorities aimed at cleaning up and humanising their grants", while insisting on the need to "prevent any abusive use, or use contrary to the interest of recipient states".

This declaration comes amid a fragile diplomatic climate. Mali, led by a military transition since 2020, recently voted against a UN resolution on Ukraine, on the same day as the DOGE announcement, as did Russia and the United States. This episode marks a new chapter of tensions between Bamako and its Western partners.

The Malian government reaffirms its commitment to peace and stability, specifying that international cooperation must take place on "the basis of mutual respect and reciprocal interests".

Towards a normalisation of relations?

Despite these tensions, Bamako appears to be leaving the door open to dialogue with Washington, notably on the question of grants. The Malian authorities' acknowledgement of the "United States' awareness of the risks of misappropriation" suggests a possibility of re-engagement under new conditions.

In the meantime, Mali remains firm on its demands: "Any future cooperation must respect the sovereignty of the Malian State and respond to the real expectations of the people."

MD/ac/Sf/APA

a7204.t:
The Bank of South Sudan has reduced its lending rate to commercial banks from 15% to 13%, in a move aimed at easing the ongoing cash crisis and boosting economic growth.
The decision was made following a meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) chaired by the central bank governor, Dr. Addis Ababa Othow.
In a statement signed by Dr. Othow and seen by Eye Radio, the central bank announced it had lowered the rate by 200 percentage points after a unanimous decision by the MPC.
“To achieve these measures, MPC revised key policy instruments and unanimously agreed to reduce the central bank rate by 200 percentage points from 15 percent to 13 percent, spur and stimulate credit to the private sector and support robust economic growth,” read part of the statement.
The bank also reviewed the Reserve Requirement Ratio (RRR). It increased the reserve ratio for deposits held in foreign currencies, such as US dollars, euros, and sterling pounds, from 20% to 25%.
However, the ratio for deposits held in South Sudanese Pounds remains at 20%.
“The MPC maintained the Reserve Requirement Ratio (RRC) for South Sudan Pound (SSP) at 20 percent of total deposits and raised the RRR for foreign currency (e.g. US dollars, Euro or Sterling Pound) from 20 percent to 25 percent of total deposits with immediate effect,” the statement continued.
“The Bank of South Sudan remains committed to supporting the economy at these tough times, and we are confident the bank sector will navigate successfully through fears and uncertainty,” the statement added.
The Bank of South Sudan last year lifted the SSP 10 million cash withdrawal limit for individual accounts, following a widespread cash shortage.
The policy shift came after weeks of a liquidity crisis that sparked public outcry.
The then Central Bank Governor, Johny Ohisa Damian, said the move was intended to encourage savings by prompting commercial banks to offer interest on savings accounts.
The change was expected to ease liquidity pressures and strengthen cooperation within the banking sector, paving the way for improved economic stability.
